about.title: Exeter Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Exeter's economy runs on agriculture, packing houses, and the small businesses that line Palm Avenue and Visalia Road, which means workplace injuries here often look different than in bigger cities — equipment accidents in the groves, forklift incidents in packing sheds, or falls at a job site near Firebaugh. In most cases, California workers' compensation is the exclusive path for injuries caused by an employer, regardless of who was at fault. But when a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, delivery driver, or another outside party contributed to the accident, you may have a separate injury claim against them. LawProactive doesn't practice law or handle claims directly — we're a free service that connects injured workers in Exeter with an independent attorney who can look at the details of what happened and explain your options, including whether a third-party claim applies alongside any workers' comp benefits you're pursuing.

whyChoose.title: Why Exeter Workers Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Third-Party Claims Aren't Always Obvious
items.desc: California law generally limits injured employees to workers' compensation against their employer, but a negligent subcontractor, property owner, or equipment maker can still be held separately liable. An independent attorney can help sort out whether that applies to your Exeter workplace incident.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Move Fast
items.desc: Employees generally have 30 days to report a workplace injury to their employer, and third-party injury claims carry their own two-year deadline under California law. Waiting to talk to someone can quietly cost you options.

items.title: Retaliation Is Illegal, and You Have Support
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from retaliating against workers who report injuries or file claims. If you're worried about speaking up, an independent attorney connected through LawProactive can walk you through your rights before you decide anything.

items.question: I work in a packing shed near Firebaugh — does workers' comp cover me even if it was my mistake?
items.answer: In most cases, yes. California workers' compensation is generally a no-fault system, meaning it usually applies regardless of who caused the accident. An independent attorney can review your specific situation to confirm how it applies and whether any third party was also involved.

items.question: What if the injury happened because of equipment made by another company?
items.answer: That's exactly the kind of situation where a third-party claim can come in alongside workers' comp. If a piece of machinery, a vehicle, or a subcontractor's negligence contributed to your injury, an independent attorney can evaluate whether you have a separate claim beyond your employer.
